security_audit.summary: Adjudicated all 235 static findings for this community skill, a Chinese-language Claude Code tutorial consisting of prose documentation (SKILL.md plus reference Markdown). Every pattern-based finding is a false positive: the matches occur inside fenced Markdown code examples (JavaScript template literals misread as shell backticks, illustrative #!/bin/bash snippets, ~/.claude config-path references, /add-dir ../sibling examples, and an 'echo $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY' troubleshooting tip) — none are code the skill executes at install or invocation time. The high-entropy heuristics reflect a large mixed-language Markdown file, not binary or encrypted content. One finding is kept at low confidence: SKILL.md's frontmatter is invalid (a stray 'TRANSLATED CONTENT:' line precedes the YAML), so it could not be statically scanned and stays flagged for manual review even though its content is benign. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md has invalid YAML frontmatter: a stray 'TRANSLATED CONTENT:' line appears on line 1, before the opening '---' delimiter, so the file cannot be statically scanned or parsed for metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the leading 'TRANSLATED CONTENT:' line so the file begins with the '---' frontmatter block. This lets automated scanning and metadata parsing succeed and clears the manual-review flag.

remediation.issue: Documentation code examples use ~/.claude and ~/.config/claude paths and example shell scripts that readers may copy and run without review.
remediation.suggestion: Add a brief note near the shell/script examples reminding readers to review commands (especially any using sudo or rm -rf) before running them, and to substitute their own paths. This is a documentation-quality improvement, not a security defect in the skill itself.

content.value_statement: Developers who read Claude Code documentation in English lack a deep Chinese-language reference for advanced features. This skill delivers a complete Chinese guide covering tools, workflows, MCP, hooks, and best practices.
actual_capabilities: Explains the seven core Claude Code tools, including the REPL, Artifacts, Web Search, and Web Fetch.
Documents advanced REPL usage with preloaded libraries such as D3.js, MathJS, and Lodash.
Describes MCP integration and how to configure external server connections.
Covers the hooks system for automating formatting, tests, and notifications.
Provides workflows for large-file analysis and multi-directory project work.
Lists troubleshooting steps and best practices for common Claude Code errors.
limitations: The content is written in Chinese, so it is best suited for Chinese-reading developers.
It is reference documentation only; it does not run code or automate any task.
Some described features are experimental or third-party and may change over time.
Details reflect the guide's writing date and may lag behind the latest official documentation.

use_cases.title: Learn Claude Code in Chinese
use_cases.description: A developer new to Claude Code reads the guide to understand the core tools and workflows in their native language.
use_cases.target_user: Chinese-speaking developers new to Claude Code

use_cases.title: Set up MCP integration
use_cases.description: An engineer follows the MCP section to connect Claude Code to an external server and use its tools.

use_cases.title: Adopt advanced workflows
use_cases.description: A team lead uses the workflow and best-practice sections to standardize how their team analyzes large files and manages tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a core tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the Claude Code guide, explain how the REPL tool works and give one simple example.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a quick overview of one tool.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize the large-file analysis workflow from the guide into three clear steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants a condensed version of a documented workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Configure MCP
prompt_templates.prompt: Based on the guide, walk me through creating a valid mcp_config.json for a Node.js MCP server.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer sets up their first MCP server.

prompt_templates.title: Design a hooks setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the hooks section of the guide, propose a settings.json that runs a formatter before edits and tests after edits, and explain each hook.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user automates their workflow with hooks.

output_examples.input: Explain the seven core Claude Code tools listed in the guide.
output_examples.output: The guide lists seven tools: REPL for running JavaScript, Artifacts for visual output, Web Search for finding information, Web Fetch for retrieving pages, Conversation Search for prior chats, Recent Chats for recent sessions, and End Conversation for cleanup.

output_examples.input: What paths does Claude Code use for configuration?
output_examples.output: The guide notes that MCP configuration lives in a Claude config file under the user home directory, and that hooks and commands are stored under a project or home Claude directory. These are shown as examples for reference.

best_practices: Read the relevant guide section before starting a task so you apply the documented workflow correctly.
Review any example command, especially those using elevated permissions, before running it yourself.
Cross-check the guide against the latest official Claude Code documentation for changed features.
anti_patterns: Copying and running example shell scripts from the guide without reading what they do.
Assuming every described feature is current, since some are experimental or may have changed.
Treating the guide as executable automation rather than reference documentation.

faq.question: What language is this guide written in?
faq.answer: The guide is written in Chinese. It is designed for developers who prefer to read documentation in Chinese.

faq.question: Does this skill run code or change my system?
faq.answer: No. It is reference documentation. It explains concepts and shows examples, but it does not execute commands on your machine.

faq.question: What topics does the guide cover?
faq.answer: It covers the core tools, the REPL environment, development workflows, MCP integration, the hooks system, advanced patterns, and best practices.

faq.question: Is this an official Anthropic guide?
faq.answer: No. It is a community guide. It combines official features with observed patterns and third-party integrations, so verify details against official documentation.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Chinese-reading developers who want to learn advanced Claude Code features and workflows will benefit most from this guide.

faq.question: Are the example commands safe to run?
faq.answer: The examples are for learning. Review each command before running it, and be careful with any command that uses elevated permissions or deletes files.
